R-038 targeted same-template-distractor experiment (R-037 follow-up): 122-query subset of the existing 500 held-out queries (miss@1 AND hit@20 AND dense top1_score >= 0.9017 [median of that 244-query distribution] -- 'dense confidently wrong but the right answer is nearby'). Same index build (data/index/metadata_aware) + embedder (E5Embedder) as A4 for direct comparability. Not written into eval/heldout_queries.json -- a derived, labeled filter only. Config B: dense top-20 candidates -> cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 rerank -> top-10, forced CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='') to match production hardware class. Fixed 15/122 rank-1 misses (0.0->0.1230 recall@1), broke 0/122 (subset is miss@1-only by construction so nothing to break AT RANK 1 specifically -- not evidence reranking is safe on already-correct queries elsewhere). But recall@5 and recall@10 both regressed sharply on this SAME subset (0.7049->0.3934, 0.9098->0.6230): the reranker promotes other same-template country-capital distractors into the top-10 window, pushing the correct-but-lower-ranked passage back out. Qualitative capital-of-India case: reranking moved 7 other countries' capital passages (Georgia/Chile/Malta/Denmark/Austria-Slovakia-Hungary/Rwanda/Uruguay) ABOVE the correct Delhi passage, which dense alone had NOT done -- reranking made the flagship motivating example worse, not better. Confirms A4's net-negative finding (full-500: recall@1 0.322->0.048, recall@5 0.652->0.228) generalizes to this targeted subset too, despite a real but modest rank-1-only benefit on some queries.

ADR-013 G3 recalibration sweep on multilingual_100k/filter candidate, 532-query held-out set. TAU=0.8835/MARGIN=0.0 KEPT UNCHANGED after evidence review -- global sweep (61 points, 0.8027-0.9527) shows precision_of_accepted flat ~0.35 across the whole range (baseline: answered=178 true_accept=62 false_accept=116 false_refusal=56 precision=0.3483; best global TAU=0.8827 only gains 178->180 answered). Per-language free-optimized TAU (rule B) looked good in aggregate (answered->204) but FAILED an even/odd query_id stability check: only 2/14 languages agree within 0.02 between halves -- overfit to n=38/language, not shipped. Normalized per-language offset rule (rule C, formula-based, cap 0.03) performed WORSE than baseline (answered->162, precision->0.315) because it raises the bar on the two best languages (hin_Deva, eng_Latn). MARGIN re-swept 0.0-0.03: precision creeps to 0.381 max while answered collapses to 97 at margin=0.03 -- MARGIN=0.0 confirmed correct pairing (matches R-015/P-015 on the old corpus). Root cause: top1 score correct-vs-wrong distributions heavily overlap (correct median=0.8846, wrong median=0.8686, wrong max=0.9463 exceeds correct median) -- a signal-quality problem, not a threshold-placement problem. See docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-013 for full rationale. Regression case (capital of India, hi+en) stays safe (abstains) under every candidate explored. Raw artifact: eval/g3_calibration_multilingual_100k_raw.json, sweep: eval/g3_threshold_sweep_multilingual_100k.json.

ADR-014 Phase 5: cheap deterministic G3 confidence-signal experiment, 532-query held-out set, no candidate adopted, TAU=0.8835/MARGIN=0.0 unchanged. 15 features + 4 combinations evaluated via AUC (hindsight-leakage-safe: gold used only to evaluate). Best individual: score_std_top5 (top-5 score std-dev) AUC=0.671 vs top1-alone AUC=0.640; gap15mean (top1-mean(top5)) AUC=0.667. Best combination: top1+concentration_ratio (top1/sum(top5)), 208 answered vs 178 baseline at precision=0.351 vs 0.348, concentration_ratio verified doing real filtering work (removes 169 candidates at 4.5:1 bad:good when top1 bar is loosened). ALL REJECTED: (1) flagship regression case (Hindi 'capital of India', top1=0.8208, wrong Bangkok/Thailand top-1 passage) is INCORRECTLY ACCEPTED by score_std_top5 and gap15mean; only the combination survives, by coincidence of that query's moderate top1; (2) that survival doesn't generalize -- 7/10 highest-top1 wrong queries in the full set fool all three candidates identically; (3) apples-to-apples new-risk count (among queries prod already abstains on) shows ~2.3-2.6 new wrong answers per 1 new correct recovered, consistently across all three candidates. Real bug found+fixed pre-emptively: Python re's \w excludes Unicode combining marks (Mn/Mc), naive \w+ tokenization shatters Devanagari/Bengali/etc at every vowel sign -- fixed before any lexical feature was built on it. same_lang_consistency AUC=0.5 exactly (legitimate null: production's hard language filter already saturates it). Per-language AUC std 0.10-0.14 for every feature; tam_Taml INVERTED for the two best-AUC features (0.388, 0.352) -- a global rule would hurt Tamil specifically. Offline logistic-regression diagnostic (numpy, train/val split by query_id parity, NOT shipped) does not generalize: train_auc=0.722 val_auc=0.632. Latency: full 15-feature bundle 535us/query (tokenization-dominated); concentration_ratio alone 1.5us/query, score_std_top5+gap15mean 19us/query -- all negligible vs 200ms budget regardless. See docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-014. Raw: eval/g3_feature_experiment_raw.json, results: eval/g3_feature_experiment_results.json.
